To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HLA class I haplotypes and genotypes are independently associated with the risk of cardiovascular morbidity and cardiovascular mortality in type 1 diabetic individuals.

the common (DRB1*10/DRB1) DQB1 05:01 haplotypes and the (DRB1 10/DRB) DQB1 *05:01/ DRB1*04 :01 DQB1 *03:02 genotype were independently associated with the risk of cardiovascular morbidity and/or death in Finnish type I diabetic patients.
HLA class 2 haplotypes and genotypes are independent risk factors for cardiovascular morbidity and/or mortality in type 1 diabetes patients with different kidney statuses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HLA class II in the development of cardiovascular disease in type 1 diabetic nephropathy.
the relationship between HLA class II genotypes and the development of atherosclerotis.
the role of HLA class II in the pathogenesis and development of atherosclerosis in type 1 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HLA class-II haplo- and genotypes are independently associated with the risk of cardiovascular events and death, especially in patients with type-1 diabetes and normal AER.
HLA class I and II genes are associated with cardiovascular disease and mortality in type 1 diabetes.
HLA II genotypes are independently associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events and death, especially in patients with normal or microalbuminuria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HLA class I haplotype (DR1/3) DQB1 *03:01/DR1*03:01/03:01/02:01 is a protective factor for cardiovascular events and mortality, while the (DR1) DQB1 05:01 haplotypes are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and death in type 1 diabetic individuals.
the (DR1-10) DQB 05:01 haplo- and (DR1- 10) DQB05:01/ DQB03:02 genotype were independent predictors of cardiovascular morbidity and/or mortality in patients with type-1 diabetes.
these two HLA class II alleles are associated with cardiovascular disease and mortality in type 1 diabetes, especially in those with microalbuminuria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HLA class I haplotypes and genotypes may influence the risk of CVD in type 1 diabetic individuals, even in those with normal renal function.

the HLA DR-DQ haplotypes and genotypes are independent risk factors for cardiovascular events and death, even after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors and the presence of kidney disease.

the HLA class II genotype (DR1/DR4, DQB1*0501/DQB1*0302) was a risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and all-cause mortality in type 1 diabetes patients with normal A1C levels and normal albuminuria, but not in those with microalbuminuria or macroalbuminuria.
